title: Essential Software Principles: YAGNI, KISS, and DRY

multi-content.title: definition
multi-content.simple-content: You Ain't Gonna Need It. Only implement functionality when it is necessary, avoiding overengineering by not adding features that may never be used.

multi-content.title: Practical Application
multi-content: Avoid implementing complex user permission systems before they're required.
Don't add configuration options until a second use case actually exists.
Skip generic abstraction layers until you have two or more concrete implementations.

multi-content.title: Common Pitfalls
multi-content: Don't use it as an excuse to skip proper design and planning.
Ignoring genuinely known requirements is not YAGNI — it is under-engineering.
Applying it to non-functional needs like security or observability, which are needed from day one.

multi-content.title: definition
multi-content.simple-content: Keep It Simple, Stupid. Design and implement solutions in a straightforward manner, minimizing complexity and unnecessary complications.

multi-content.title: Practical Application
multi-content: Choose a straightforward authentication approach before considering OAuth federation.
Prefer a readable loop over a dense one-liner that needs a comment to explain it.
Reach for a library or framework feature only when hand-rolled code has become the harder option.

multi-content.title: Common Pitfalls
multi-content: Simple doesn't mean incomplete or poorly designed.
Over-simplifying can push complexity onto the caller instead of removing it.
Confusing 'few lines of code' with 'easy to understand'.

multi-content.title: definition
multi-content.simple-content: Don't Repeat Yourself. Avoid duplication in code by abstracting common logic into reusable components, ensuring maintainability and reducing errors.

multi-content.title: Practical Application
multi-content: Create utility classes for common validation logic used across controllers.
Centralize configuration values rather than repeating literals across modules.
Extract shared test setup into fixtures or builders.

multi-content.title: Common Pitfalls
multi-content: Don't over-abstract code to the point of confusion.
Coincidental duplication is not real duplication — two pieces of code that look alike today may change for different reasons tomorrow.
Coupling unrelated modules through a shared helper just to remove a few repeated lines.

multi-content.title: description
multi-content.simple-content: These principles are guidelines for judgement, not rules to apply mechanically. They earn their keep at specific decision points.

multi-content.title: Moments That Call for Them
multi-content: When starting a new feature or component.
During code refactoring sessions.
When reviewing pull requests.
When making architectural decisions.

multi-content.title: Holding Them in Tension
multi-content: DRY and KISS can conflict: removing duplication sometimes adds indirection. Favour the option a new reader would understand faster.
YAGNI and DRY can conflict: don't build a shared abstraction for a second use case that doesn't exist yet.
When two principles disagree, the tiebreaker is the cost of changing the code later.
